title: Process, Outcome & Self-Worth

launchpad.outcome: Grade outcome, process and strategy separately, and keep one trade as one observation.
launchpad.missionQuestion: What does this trade actually tell me?

cards:
2 · PROCESS QUALITY
did I follow my rules?
lines: WIN ≠ GOOD TRADE. LOSS ≠ BAD TRADE.

slides.title: Two trades

trades.name: TRADE A
facts: Entered at the first valid retest.
trades.why: One valid loss says nothing about the strategy yet.

trades.name: TRADE B
trades.why: A win from a rule violation isn’t evidence that the method was executed.

slides.punch: JUDGE THE BEHAVIOR QUICKLY. JUDGE THE STRATEGY SLOWLY.

slides.title: Write the state down, not just the trade

example.plannedResponse: Pause and require the full checklist

asks.prompt: In this example, which field turns the feeling into a decision?

options.label: PLANNED RESPONSE
options.why: Decided now, used later: in the journal, the pre-trade planner and the simulator.

slides.punch: Private to you. Never shared, never ranked.

slides.title: Self-worth, kept simple

asks.prompt: IS THIS ENOUGH DATA TO DEFINE YOUR SKILL?

options.label: NO
options.why: Not your skill, and definitely not who you are.

slides.punch: One trade is one observation. Not identity.

slides.quote: Your P&L grades the trade. Your journal grades the process. Neither one grades you.

slides.prompt: What does “judge behavior quickly, judge strategy slowly” mean?
slides.modelAnswer: After every trade I can say right away whether I followed my rules. But whether the strategy works takes a meaningful sample. One win or loss can’t answer that.

remember: JUDGE THE BEHAVIOR QUICKLY. JUDGE THE STRATEGY SLOWLY.
